boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the complete one-engagement frozen source campaign. The January 4/5 arrival discrepancy and matched opening populations remain unresolved; neither tactical nor campaign replacement boundaries are established. Prose claims supply no admitted model features.

claims.value: Allan describes Jackson leaving Winchester on January 1 with some eight or nine thousand men, including multiple brigades, militia, batteries and cavalry.
claims.rationale: An explicitly approximate retrospective expedition total. It does not count the opening Hancock population or the Union garrison. The later footnote listing formations found at Hancock after the engagement is not an opening return.

citations.locator: Chapter I, Romney; p.20, paragraph beginning Such was the condition of affairs (OCR pagination, unverified against scan)
citations.quote: the whole numbering some eight or nine thousand (8000 or 9000) men.

claims.rationale: The frozen side-specific strength bounds are blank. Neither the NPS summary nor Allan’s expedition estimate establishes matched opening strengths, detachment membership or a common boundary for Hancock.

claims.value: The current NPS page displays zero troops on both sides and a January 1862 date field; the frozen row dates the engagement January 5–6.
claims.rationale: Displayed zeros and the campaign-like month do not supply measured personnel or exact engagement timing. Preserve both sources without replacing missing strength with zero.

claims.value: NPS places Jackson opposite Hancock on January 5 and describes unsuccessful efforts to find a safe crossing. Allan places the main force opposite Hancock on the night of January 4 and describes an attempted bridge above the town.
claims.rationale: The river separates positions, but the sources disagree about the arrival date. Retain the discrepancy without creating a common opening clock or silently changing the frozen interval. Allan’s bridge narrative is a retrospective assertion, not a verified engineering survey or contemporary knowledge record.

citations.quote: On January 5, after skirmishing with the retiring Federals, Jackson's force reached the Potomac River opposite the garrisoned town of Hancock, Maryland.
Jackson continued the bombardment for two days while unsuccessfully searching for a safe river crossing.

citations.quote: The main Confederate force bivouacked on the night of the 4th opposite Hancock.

citations.locator: Chapter I, Romney; p.22, same paragraph (OCR pagination, unverified against scan)
citations.quote: an eifort was made to construct a bridge at a point two miles above, wath the view of crossing to the Maryland side.

claims.value: Allan describes wagons delayed by difficult roads during the approach, leaving troops without food and in some cases covering on the second night, followed by a renewed separation of wagons and troops in snow and sleet.
claims.rationale: These are attributed conditions before the Hancock engagement, not quantified January 5 readiness, an invented morale score or a reviewed causal effect. All inherited/created classifications remain unresolved until replacement boundaries are established. OCR spelling is preserved in the quotation.

citations.locator: Chapter I, Romney; p.21, approach/weather paragraph (OCR pagination, unverified against scan)
citations.quote: the troops passed the night without anything to eat,^ and, in many cases, without covering.

citations.locator: Chapter I, Romney; p.21, same paragraph (OCR pagination, unverified against scan)
citations.quote: Snow and sleet during the latter part of the day added much to the discomfort of the soldiers, and rendered the roads so slippery that the wagons were again unable to keep up with the troops.

claims.rationale: No original reconnaissance, surrender correspondence, engineering report or message chain was inspected to establish the commanders’ contemporary information. Allan’s inference about anticipated reinforcements is not an independently verified knowledge state. The targeted original-report follow-up was inaccessible.

claims.value: The NPS summary describes Jackson’s initial objective as disrupting the B&O Railroad and C&O Canal.
claims.rationale: A retrospective summary of the operation’s aim, not an inspected pre-march directive or a quantitative measure of campaign contribution. Later damage elsewhere does not become a second modeled Hancock success.

citations.quote: with the objective of disrupting traffic on the B&O Railroad and C&O Canal.

claims.value: NPS attributes the surrender demand to Jackson and its refusal to Lander. Allan describes Lander as having just arrived and assumed command at Hancock.
claims.rationale: These are source-attributed actions and a retrospective command sequence, not a verified transfer time or allocation of all outcome credit. The two families are not proven independent.

citations.quote: Union garrison commander Brig. Gen. F.W. Lander refused Jackson's demands for surrender.

citations.quote: Gen. Lander had just arrived and assumed command at Hancock, and he refused to surrender

claims.rationale: Preserve the nondecisive source labels without converting them to a win, half-win or validated tactical effect.

claims.value: The pinned table gives 25 total casualties; the live NPS table displays zero total and zero on each side.
claims.rationale: The live display does not adjudicate the pinned number, and no checked return resolves this discrepancy. Neither count is a strength estimate, a readiness measure or a predictor.

claims.value: NPS says the Confederates withdrew toward Romney on January 7; Allan likewise places departure from the Hancock vicinity on the morning of the 7th.
claims.rationale: This is later context beyond the frozen January 5–6 record. Do not merge the rest of the Romney expedition into this engagement, enlarge the frozen campaign membership, or add a second performance score.

Original reports/returns, the January 4/5 approach discrepancy, and the 25-versus-zero casualty fields remain deferred after the single targeted follow-up. Allan’s OCR has not been checked against print.
Keep the January 7 withdrawal and the wider Romney operation as context unless a separately justified campaign definition is reviewed; preserve the frozen frame meanwhile.
